source: For constant speed, distance equals speed multiplied by elapsed time. Mira moves at 3 metres per second; Noor moves at 5. Both share the same elapsed time. Noor adds 2 more metres each second, so the gap grows by 2 metres for each second that passes.

Read the full explanation without the controls

Distance = speed × elapsed time. At 6 seconds, Mira has travelled 3 × 6 = 18 metres. Noor has travelled 5 × 6 = 30 metres. Their gap is 30 − 18 = 12 metres.

Noor travels 2 more metres each second, so gap = (5 − 3) × time = 2 × time. This holds because both start together, move in the same direction, and keep constant speed.

Useful static values
Time	Mira, 3 m/s	Noor, 5 m/s	Gap
0 s	0 m	0 m	0 m
4 s	12 m	20 m	8 m
6 s	18 m	30 m	12 m
12 s	36 m	60 m	24 m
